workEn: The Secret History of the Mongols
title: 元朝秘史 §§254–254
titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §254: Jesüi Speaks, and Kökösös Reproves Cha'adai
part: §254 — Jesüi Speaks, and Kökösös Reproves Cha'adai
source: Mongγol-un niγuča tobčiyan (The Secret History of the Mongols), §§254–254, in the Ming Chinese-character phonetic transcription, as edited with a romanized reading by Shiratori Kurakichi 白鳥庫吉, 音訳蒙文元朝秘史 (Tokyo, 1943), itself based on the Ye Dehui 葉德輝 printed edition of 1905/1908; text taken from the Japanese Wikisource transcription, archived and verified against it character for character. Shiratori died in 1942, so the edition was public domain in Japan before the URAA date and was never restored in the United States. Section numbering (§) is the standard citation system. Romanization convention: Shiratori's, kept exactly as he prints it (γ, ġ, ṅ, ž, č, and the raised dot of γ̇). Translations are made fresh from the Mongolian, with the Ming interlinear Chinese glosses as the primary crib. No modern translation was consulted. langCode is null: there is no text-to-speech for Middle Mongol.
about: Before the march against the Sartaul people, Lady Jesüi presses Chinggis on who is to come after him (the glosses leave the exact sense uncertain; §254). Chinggis admits he had forgotten the question of his own death, and asks his eldest son Jüchi to speak; Cha'adai, cutting in, insults Jüchi, and the two come to blows until Kökösös rebukes Cha'adai with a long speech on the lawless age before the rising and on their mother's hardships. Grammar to watch: the paired similes with metü ‘like’; reciprocal -ldu- in olžalaldun, körüleldün, bulγalduqui; the conditional -γ̇asu / -ġesü (Ming 呵); the reflexive -(i)jen/-(i)jan; and the long speech, which the Ming glossators carry in one unbroken quotation.
draftNote: The Mongol readings follow Shiratori throughout; the English is a first drafting.

sentences.t: Teġün-ü qoina Čiṅgis Qaγan Sartaγ̇ul irgen-e Uquna teriġüten žaγ̇un elčin(i)-jen žedgüžü alaγdažu

morph.gloss: that (stem teġün- before case endings) [那的]
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
the Sartaul, a people (the Ming 囘囘 ‘Muslims’) [囘囘]
plural possessive: ‘those headed by him’, and the rest (uncertain)
reflexive-possessive: one’s own (front-vowel form, the (i) is Shiratori’s)
to obstruct, block (stem inferred from the Ming) [阻當着]

sentences.l: That-of after, Chinggis Qaγan, Sartaul people-by, Uquna and-the-headed hundred envoys-his-own, blocking, being-killed,
sentences.i: Afterwards, his envoys, Uquna and the hundred with him, had been obstructed and killed by the Sartaul people, and Chinggis Qahan
sentences.n: Read the opening as a long subject-chain whose verb is ügülerün ‘saying’ in the next unit: the envoys (Uquna and a hundred) are the ones obstructed and killed, and the Sartaul people are the agent. Alaγdažu is ala- ‘kill’ + passive -γda- + converb -žu (Ming 被殺着 ‘being killed’), and irgen-e then carries the agent sense ‘by the Sartaul people’ (as with a passive elsewhere in the text); the Ming 百姓行 only marks the dative-locative. Sartaγ̇ul is the Ming’s 囘囘 ‘Muslims’. Teriġüten (teriġü ‘head’ + -ten, Ming 等 ‘and the rest’) is uncertain in its fine sense. žedgüžü (Ming 阻當着 ‘obstructing, blocking’) is a stem I infer from the Ming; it carries no passive marker and the Ming gives it as active, so ‘obstructed’ in `i` is the sense of the whole chain (the envoys are the ones blocked), not a form of the verb.

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan ügülerün: "Altan arγamži-jan Sartaγ̇ul irgen-e ker tasuldan büleġei" keġen

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
Altan, ‘gold’; here the Jin emperor’s title (Altan Qaγan), shortened [金]
leash, leading-rope (Ming 縻繩) [縻繩 自的行]
the Sartaul, a people (the Ming 囘囘 ‘Muslims’) [囘囘]
to cut off (stem inferred from the Ming 敎斷) [敎斷]

sentences.l: Chinggis Qaγan saying: "Altan leash-own Sartaul people-to how cut-off was" saying,
sentences.i: said, “How was it that the Sartaul people were cut loose from the Altan’s own leash?” and then
sentences.n: Quotation opens with Altan and closes at büleġei". This sentence is the hardest in the part, and I give it only as a reading. Arγamži (Ming 縻繩 ‘leading-rope, tether’) + reflexive -(i)jan is the Altan Qan’s own tether on the Sartaul; tasuldan is tasul- ‘cut off’ (inferred from Ming 敎斷, literally ‘cause to cut’) + -dan; the passive ‘were cut loose’ in `i` is my reading, a causative (‘how had they it cut’) being just as possible; büleġei is ‘used to be’. Whether it means ‘how did the Sartaul people come to be cut loose?’ or something nearer ‘how could they have cut us off?’ I cannot settle from the glosses. Altan is Ming 金 (Jin), taken as short for the Altan Qaγan. The closing keġen (‘saying’) belongs to this quote.

sentences.t: Uquna teriġüten žaγ̇un elčin-ü-ġen ösül ösen kisal kisan Sartaγ̇ul irgen-dür morilaja" keġen

morph.gloss: plural possessive: ‘those headed by him’, and the rest (uncertain)
the Sartaul, a people (the Ming 囘囘 ‘Muslims’) [囘囘]

sentences.l: Uquna and-the-headed hundred envoys-own, enmity avenging, grievance requiting, Sartaul people-against let-us-mount" saying,
sentences.i: “Let us mount against the Sartaul people, avenge the wrong done to my envoys, Uquna and the hundred with him, and requite the grudge,” he said.
sentences.n: Second quotation: Shiratori prints no opening mark before Uquna; I supply it in `i` only. Elčin-ü-ġen is the genitive plus the reflexive, ‘of (my) own envoys’, which is why `i` has ‘the wrong done to my envoys’. Ösül ösen and kisal kisan are paired noun + verb-form phrases (Ming 讐報, 仇報, ‘avenge the enmity, requite the grudge’); the verbs ösen and kisan I read as converb-or-participle forms of öse-/ösü- and kisa-, with the stems inferred from the Ming. Morilaja is mori ‘horse’ + -la- ‘ride’ + hortative -ja ‘let us’ (Ming 上馬咱). Irgen-dür is ‘against/to the people’ (Ming 百姓行).

sentences.t: morilaqui-dur tende Jesüi Qatun Čiṅgis Qaγ̇an-a duradγan öčirün

words.reading: 秣舌驪剌(中灰)-突︀舌兒 morilaqui-dur

morph.gloss: lady, queen, wife of a qan [娘子]
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
to say to a superior, report [奏]

sentences.l: Mounting at, there Jesüi Qatun, Chinggis Qaγan-to reminding, reporting:
sentences.i: As they were about to mount, Lady Jesüi reminded Chinggis Qahan and said to him:
sentences.n: Jesüi is the Ming’s ‘woman’s name’ (婦人名); she is a qatun, ‘lady, wife of a qan’. Duradγan (Ming 提 ‘bring up, mention’) is the converb of duradγa- (‘recall, mention’), and öčirün is öči- ‘say to a superior’ (Ming 奏 ‘report to the throne’) + -rün; the Ming 行 on Qaγ̇an-a is the dative ‘to’. Morilaqui-dur is the participle + dative-locative, ‘at the time of mounting’ (Ming 上馬時).

sentences.t: Qaγan ündür dabaγ̇a daban örgen müred ketülün urtu čaγ̇ur čaγ̇uran olon ulus(i)-jan žibšiġerün sedkibe.

morph.gloss: to put in order (stem inferred from the Ming 整治) [整治]

sentences.l: Qaγan high pass crossing, wide rivers fording, long marching marching, many people-own ordering, thought.
sentences.i: “Qahan, crossing high passes and fording wide rivers, on long marches, and setting your many peoples in order, you have given thought:
sentences.n: Jesüi’s speech begins here; Shiratori prints no opening mark, so `i` supplies it and the speech runs on to medetügei" (the unit that closes it, ‘Žarliγ medetügei’). A converb chain: daban, ketülün and čaγ̇uran are converbs in -n and žibšiġerün is a converb in -rün; their verb is sedkibe ‘thought’. Čaγ̇ur čaγ̇uran (Ming 征, 征進) pairs a noun with its converb, ‘marching, a-marching’. Dabaγ̇a is ‘pass’ (Ming 嶺 ‘ridge’). Žibšiġe- (Ming 整治 ‘put in order’) is a stem I infer from the Ming. The unit is a reading of the chain; the parts are clear, the full sense (‘given thought to what comes after you’) is carried by the following units.

sentences.t: Töregsen ele amitan-dur müṅke ügei ažuγ̇u.
sentences.l: Born, indeed, living-beings-among eternal without was.
sentences.i: Of all that is born, indeed, among living beings there is none that is eternal.
sentences.n: Töregsen is the participle of töre- ‘be born’ (Ming 生了的); ele ‘indeed, only’ (Ming 但); amitan-dur ‘among living things’ (Ming 生靈每行, the dative-locative -dur). ‘Müṅke ügei ažuγ̇u’ is ‘there was no eternity’, the past of a- ‘be’ read here as a general truth. Müṅke is the word that also names Möngke the man; here it is the adjective ‘eternal’ (Ming 長生).

sentences.t: Neġüle metü beje čin-u negüs oduγ̇asu nedkel metü ulus(i)-jan ken-e gemü.

morph.gloss: genitive: your (on the oblique stem čin-)
to topple, fall (Ming 傾; formation uncertain) [傾]
is, exists (Ming 委有; form uncertain) [委有]

sentences.l: Old-tree like body your falling if-goes, tangled-hemp like people-own whom-to is.
sentences.i: If your body, like an old tree, should fall, to whom would your people, like tangled hemp, be left?
sentences.n: A simile pair, built on metü ‘like’ (Ming 般) and the conditional -uγ̇asu (‘if’, Ming 呵). Neġüle is a word I cannot place (Ming gives 大木 ‘big tree’; the glossary has it as ‘old tree’, uncertain), and negüs is read from the Ming 傾 ‘lean, topple’. Nedkel is Ming 麻穰, tangled hemp. Gemü (Ming 委有) closes the clause; ken-e is ‘to whom?’, and I take the whole as a rhetorical question, ‘who will have them?’ (‘be left’ in `i` is my wording); the Ming leaves the exact sense of gemü open.

sentences.t: Tulu metü beje čin-u tulbas oduγ̇asu tujal metü ulus(i)-jan ken-e gemü.

morph.gloss: pillar-foot (Ming 柱腳; word uncertain) [柱腳]
genitive: your (on the oblique stem čin-)
to topple (Ming 倒; formation uncertain) [倒]
flock of birds (Ming 羣鳥; word uncertain) [羣鳥]
is, exists (Ming 委有; form uncertain) [委有]

sentences.l: Pillar-foot like body your falling if-goes, flock-of-birds like people-own whom-to is.
sentences.i: If your body, like a pillar base, should topple, to whom would your people, like a scattered flock of birds, be left?
sentences.n: Parallel to the sentence before: tulu is a pillar’s foot (Ming 柱腳), tulbas ‘topple’ (Ming 倒; the stem is uncertain), and tujal a flock of birds (Ming 羣鳥). The Ming glosses tulbas 倒 as it glossed negüs 傾, so the two are near-synonyms. ‘Be left’ is my wording of the open gemü. ‘Scattered’ is my addition to ‘flock’, as the sense of the image, not a word of the text.

sentences.t: Töregsen dörben külüġüd köġüd(ü)-ġen ken-e in-ü keġemü.
sentences.l: Born four heroes sons-own whom-to his says.
sentences.i: Of the four heroic sons born to you, which one do you say is to have it?
sentences.n: Here the sense is the least certain of Jesüi’s question. Dörben ‘four’ with külüġüd ‘heroes’ (külüg ‘swift, outstanding’ + plural -d; Ming 俊傑每) and köġüd(ü)-ġen ‘own sons’; ken-e ‘to whom’; in-ü is ‘his’ (Ming 他的) and keġemü ‘says’ (Ming 說有). ‘Which one … to have it’ is my reading, supplying the inheritance the next units make plain; literally the Mongol is only ‘to whom, his, he says’.

sentences.t: köġüd-te deġü-ner-e olon qaračus-a man-a ber maγ̇un-a uqažu aquj-a uqaγsan(i)-jan duradγaγsan bolba.

morph.gloss: to understand [省得了的 自的行]

words.reading: 都︀舌剌惕中合黑三 duradγaγsan

sentences.l: Sons-to, younger-brothers-to, many commoners-to, us-to also, the-bad-ones-to, understanding being-while, understood-mentioned became.
sentences.i: Being aware, you have brought up what you understood before your sons, your younger brothers, the many common people, and us as well, and even the bad.
sentences.n: The Ming reads maγ̇un-a as 歹每行 ‘to the bad ones’; ‘the bad’ keeps to the Ming ‘bad ones’. Uqažu aquj-a, ‘being aware’ (Ming 省着 有行), opens the clause in `i`. Man-a is ‘to us’ (exclusive ba, oblique man-; Ming 俺). Qaračus is the commoners (qaračus ‘common people’, Ming 下民), and aquj-a (Ming 有行) is a-/bü- ‘be’ + -qui + dative -a, ‘while being’. Uqaγsan(i)-jan duradγaγsan bolba is the participle of uqa- ‘understand’ + reflexive, then the participle of duradγa- ‘mention’ + bolba ‘became’: ‘it came about that you mentioned what you understood’ — my reading from Ming 省得了的 自的行 提說了的 做了. I could not settle how the datives bind to the verbs; I take them all as the audience.

sentences.t: Žarliγ medetügei" keġen öčiġešü

morph.gloss: to say to a superior, report [奏呵]

sentences.l: Decree let-him-know" saying, reporting-when,
sentences.i: Let your decree be known.” So she said, and when she had reported,
sentences.n: Closes Jesüi’s speech at medetügei". Medetügei is mede- ‘know’ + optative -tügei (‘let it be known’; Ming 知者); žarliγ ‘command’ (Ming 聖旨, imperial decree). Öčiġešü is öči- ‘report’ + conditional -ġesü (Ming 奏呵), so ‘when/if she reported’. I take the Ming’s sense as ‘let the decree be known’, the same formula as at the end of Jüchi’s speech (where `i` reads it the same way); who is to know it, and how, the Ming does not say.

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan žarliγ bolurun:

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.l: Chinggis Qaγan decree when-issuing:
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan then issued a decree:
sentences.n: Žarliγ bolurun is ‘as he made a command’, bol- ‘become’ + -urun (Ming 做的); I follow the house rendering žarliγ bolurun → ‘issued a decree’.

sentences.t: "Qatun ber küġün böġesü Jesüi-jin üge žöb-eče žöb

morph.gloss: lady, queen, wife of a qan [娘子]
Jesüi, a woman’s name [婦人名的]

sentences.l: "Lady also person being-if, Jesüi-of word right-from right.
sentences.i: “Though she is a lady, she is a person, and Jesüi’s word is right — indeed right.
sentences.n: Chinggis’s decree. Shiratori’s opening mark sits before Qatun. Qatun ber küġün böġesü: ber ‘even, also’ with the conditional böġesü (Ming 有呵) gives ‘even a lady, if (she) be a person’ — the force is ‘a lady is still a person’ (my reading). Žöb-eče žöb: žöb ‘right, correct’ + ablative -eče (Ming 是上 ‘on the ground that it is right’), then žöb again, ‘right from its being right’, a doubled assertion. Jesüi-jin is the name + genitive after a vowel.

sentences.t: ked-ber deġü-ner köġüd ta ber Boγ̇orču Muqali-tan ein ese duradγaba.
sentences.l: Whichever younger-brothers, sons, you also, Bo'orchu, Muqali and-others thus not mentioned.
sentences.i: None of you, whether younger brothers or sons, nor you, Bo'orchu, Muqali and the rest, had spoken of it so.
sentences.n: Ked-ber (Ming 任誰每, ‘whoever’) is ked ‘how many, whichever’ + ber ‘even’; with the following ese ‘not’ (negating a past act), ‘not one of … had mentioned’. Ta is the plural polite ‘you’; Muqali-tan is Muqali + -tan ‘and the like’ (Ming 等). Ein ‘thus’ (Ming 這般) – ‘had said it thus’, i.e. as Jesüi did. Duradγaba is the past of duradγa- ‘mention’.

sentences.t: Bi ber uridus-i ülü udaγ̇araqui-ača umartažu ažuγ̇u.

words.reading: 兀荅阿舌剌(中灰)-阿察 udaγ̇araqui-ača

morph.gloss: to follow behind (stem inferred) [隨後的 行]

sentences.l: I also forebears not following-from forgetting was.
sentences.i: I too had been forgetting the forebears, not looking to what comes after;
sentences.n: Chinggis’s admission. Uridus (Ming 祖宗每 ‘ancestors’) is the plural of uridu ‘earlier’, here the accusative -i; udaγ̇araqui-ača (Ming 隨後的 行) is a participle with an ablative, ‘from not following behind’. I take the sense as ‘not thinking of what must follow’, but the Ming gloss 隨後 ‘follow after’ allows other readings. Umartažu ažuγ̇u is the converb + past of a-: ‘was forgetting’.

sentences.t: Üküküj-e ülü erüsteküj-eče untaražu ažuγ̇u"

morph.gloss: to die (stem from the Ming 死) [死的行]

words.reading: 額舌魯思帖古耶徹 erüsteküj-eče

morph.gloss: to be overtaken, caught (stem inferred; Ming 被得着) [被得着]

sentences.l: Dying not being-overtaken sleeping was."
sentences.i: not thinking of dying, not of being overtaken; I had been asleep.”
sentences.n: Both are participles in -küj (üküküj-e Ming 死的行, from ükü- ‘die’; erüsteküj-eče Ming 被得着), but the sense of their cases is not clear; both take the sense ‘not (thinking) of …’ from the repeated ülü. Untaražu ažuγ̇u (Ming 睡着着 有來) is ‘sleeping, was’: ‘I had been asleep’. Closes Chinggis’s quote.

sentences.t: keġeġed köġüd-ün min-u aqa Žüči bi-že.
sentences.l: Having-said: sons-of my eldest Jüchi is-indeed.
sentences.i: After he had said this, he went on: “The eldest of my sons is Jüchi.
sentences.n: Shiratori prints no opening mark before köġüd-ün; I supply it in `i`. The quotation runs to kelele" two units on. Aqa ‘elder brother’ is used as an adjective ‘eldest’ (Ming 長); bi-že (Ming 有也者) is bü- ‘be’ (stem bi-) + the assertion particle -že, ‘indeed is’.

sentences.t: Jaγ̇u keġemü.
sentences.l: What says.
sentences.i: What do you say?
sentences.n: Jaγ̇u ‘what’ (Ming 甚), keġemü ‘says’ (Ming 說有). keġemü has no person ending, so ‘you’ in `i` rests on my reading that Chinggis asks it of his son Jüchi, whom the next unit bids speak; the Mongol does not name the person asked.

sentences.t: či kelele" keġebe.
sentences.l: You speak" he-said.
sentences.i: You speak!” he said.
sentences.n: Closes Chinggis’s quote (kelele"). Kelele is kele- ‘speak’ + the imperative -le (the glossary’s ‘form uncertain’), and keġebe closes the quote with ‘said’.

sentences.t: Žüči-ji doṅγodqu-jin urida Čaγ̇adai ügülerün:

morph.gloss: to give voice, speak out (stem inferred from Ming 作聲) [作聲的]

sentences.l: Jüchi-(object) speaking-of before Cha'adai saying:
sentences.i: Before Jüchi spoke, Cha'adai said:
sentences.n: Doṅγodqu-jin urida (Ming 作聲的 前) is the participle ‘one who gives voice’ + genitive, + ‘before’: ‘before the speaking one’. The stem doṅγod- (‘give voice’) is inferred from the Ming. Žüči-ji is Jüchi + accusative -ji after a vowel, which I read as the object of a lost verb or as part of a noun phrase ‘Jüchi’s speaking’ — Ming 人名行 ‘to Jüchi’. Unsure.

sentences.t: "Žüči-ji kelele keġerün Žüči-(j)üġü tüšin ügülemüi.

morph.gloss: to entrust, rely on (stem inferred from Ming 委付) [委付]

sentences.l: "Jüchi-(object) speak" when-saying, Jüchi-(question) entrusting says.
sentences.i: “When you say ‘Jüchi, speak!’ — do you mean to give it into Jüchi’s hands?
sentences.n: Cha'adai’s speech begins: the opening mark is Shiratori’s and the closing mark is at bida" in the next unit. Žüči-(j)üġü is Jüchi + the question particle -üġü (Ming 麽) after the object. Tüšin is tüši- ‘entrust’ (stem inferred; Ming 委付) in converb -n. Ügülemüi is ‘says’ (Ming 說有), here ‘do you say, mean’. I write ‘into Jüchi’s hands’ as a gloss on tüšin; the verb has no object printed.

sentences.t: Ene Merkidai Čulγ̇ul žaγ̇ura ker medeġülkün bida" keġeküi-lüġe

morph.gloss: Chulgul, a people (Ming 種名), perhaps a Merkid clan [(種名)]
comitative: together with, at the moment of

sentences.l: This Merkid, Chulgul among how be-managed we" at-saying,
sentences.i: How are we to have it managed, amid this Merkid, this Chulgul?” — at the very moment he spoke,
sentences.n: Cha'adai’s insult. Merkidai is the Merkid people (Ming 種名) plus an ending -ai of uncertain force (‘a Merkid man’?), and Čulγ̇ul (Ming 種名) is marked as another people, perhaps a Merkid clan; žaγ̇ura is ‘midst, among’ (Ming 其間). Ker medeġülkün bida (Ming 怎生 敎策 咱) I read as ‘how shall we (inclusive) have it managed/counselled?’, mede- ‘manage’ + causative + -kün (the Ming 敎策 ‘cause to plan’ does not itself say ‘rule’). The words are clear; the target of the insult is a matter for history, not for these glosses, and I leave it so. Keġeküi-lüġe is keġe- ‘say’ + participle -küi + comitative -lüġe, ‘at the moment of saying’ (Ming 恰說呵).

sentences.t: Žüči bosuγ̇ad Čaγ̇adai-jin žaqa-dur tusču ügülerün:

morph.gloss: to arrive, reach (stem inferred from the Ming 到着) [到着]

sentences.l: Jüchi rising, Cha'adai-of collar-at arriving saying:
sentences.i: Jüchi rose, took Cha'adai by the collar, and said:
sentences.n: Žaqa-dur (Ming 領行) is ‘at the collar’; tusču (Ming 到着) is tus- ‘arrive’ + converb -ču, ‘reaching’. The Ming’s 領行 is a dative here and the reading ‘seized him by the collar’ is mine; the Mongol says ‘arriving at the collar of Cha'adai’. Žaqāča (in the unit eight later) is the same word with the ablative.

sentences.t: "Qān ečige-de busu ese keġegdelüġe.

morph.gloss: qan, ruler, sovereign (the short form) [皇帝]

sentences.l: "Qan father-to other not has-been-said.
sentences.i: “Father Qan has not called me an outsider.
sentences.n: Jüchi’s answer (quote opens at Qān). Keġegdelüġe is keġe- ‘say’ + passive -gde- + past -lüġe (Ming 被說來 ‘was said’), and the Ming is ‘by Father Qan, other (busu), not has it been said’. I read busu ‘other’ as ‘an outsider’, i.e. ‘not a stranger’: Jüchi’s father has never told him he is not of the family. Uncertain; ‘Qān ečige’ is Chinggis, as ‘Father Qan’ (house rendering).

sentences.t: Či nama-ji ker ilγamui.
sentences.l: You me-(object) how distinguish.
sentences.i: How do you set me apart?
sentences.n: Ilγamui is ilγa- ‘distinguish, sort’ (Ming 分揀 ‘sort out’) + present -mui; nama-ji is ‘me, as object’ (bi, stem nama-, accusative -ji).

sentences.t: Ambar erdem(i)-ġer hüleġü či.

morph.gloss: what (Ming 甚麼, sense uncertain) [甚麽]

words.reading: 額舌兒迭米-額舌兒 erdem(i)-ġer

sentences.l: What skill-by superior you.
sentences.i: By what skill are you the better?
sentences.n: Ambar (Ming 甚麼) is ‘what’ in the glossary but nowhere else known; erdem is erdem ‘skill’ (Ming 技能), erdem(i)-ġer the instrumental -ġer (Ming 敎 ‘cause’) with Shiratori’s (i). Hüleġü ‘surplus, greater’ (Ming 勝, also 多餘); či ‘you’ — I read ‘you are greater by what skill?’

sentences.t: Γaγča kečeġü-ber(i)-jen maqa hüleġü ele či.

morph.gloss: tough, hard (stem uncertain; Ming 剛) [剛敎自的(行)]

sentences.l: Only toughness-own perhaps greater indeed you.
sentences.i: Perhaps it is only by your own toughness that you are greater — you alone.
sentences.n: Kečeġü-ber(i)-jen is kečeġü ‘toughness’ (Ming 剛 ‘hard, firm’, with no sense of blame; glossary-unknown, from the Ming 剛敎) + instrumental -ber + reflexive -(i)jen. Maqa (Ming 莫) ‘perhaps (not)’ puts the clause as a doubting question. Hüleġü ele či: ‘greater only you’. Uncertain throughout.

sentences.t: Hontučažu čima-da γardaγ̇asu heregei-jen hoγtolžu oγ̇orsuγai.

morph.gloss: to shoot from afar (stem inferred) [賽遠射着]
dative-locative: at, to you (oblique stem čima-)
to throw away (stem inferred; Ming 丟) [丟我]

sentences.l: Distant-shooting you-to if-I-am-beaten, thumb-own cutting-off may-I-throw-away.
sentences.i: If I am beaten by you in a contest of shooting afar, let me cut off my thumb and throw it away.
sentences.n: Hontučažu (Ming 賽遠射着 ‘contesting at shooting afar’) is a converb of hontuča- (stem inferred). γardaγ̇asu (Ming 被勝呵) is a passive in -da- (cf. -γda- in ilaγdaγ̇asu below) of a stem γar- ‘overcome’, not the γar- ‘go out’ of other units, with the conditional -γ̇asu; I take it as ‘if (I) am beaten’. Heregei is the thumb (Ming 大拇指), hoγtolžu ‘cutting off’; oγ̇orsuγai (Ming 丟我) is a first-person optative ‘let me throw it away’. Čima-da is ‘to/at you’.

sentences.t: Abaldužu čima-da ilaγdaγ̇asu umaγsan γažar-ača bu bossuγai.

morph.gloss: to wrestle, grapple (stem inferred from the Ming 相搏着, uncertain) [相搏着]
dative-locative: at, to you (oblique stem čima-)

sentences.l: Wrestling you-to if-I-am-beaten, fallen place-from not may-I-rise.
sentences.i: If I lose to you at wrestling, let me not rise from the spot where I have fallen.
sentences.n: Abaldu- is aba- ‘grapple’ + reciprocal -ldu- (Ming 相搏 ‘fight hand to hand’, ‘seize one another’); ilaγdaγ̇asu (Ming 被勝呵) is ila- ‘win’ + passive -γda- + conditional, ‘if I am beaten’. Umaγsan is the participle of una- ‘fall’ (written umaγ-; Ming 倒了的). Bu bossuγai: bu ‘not’ (the prohibitive) + bos- ‘rise’ + optative -suγai; Ming 休 起者 ‘let me not rise’.

sentences.t: Qān ečige-jin žarliγ medetügei" keġebe.

morph.gloss: qan, ruler, sovereign (the short form) [皇帝]

sentences.l: Qan father-of decree let-it-be-known" he-said.
sentences.i: Let the decree of Father Qan be known.” So he spoke.
sentences.n: Closes Jüchi’s speech. Medetügei ‘let it be known’ repeats the words that closed Jesüi’s speech; I read it as Jüchi calling on the Qan’s ruling to stand witness to his offer, but the Ming (知者) says only ‘let it be known’.

sentences.t: Žüči Čaγ̇adai qojar žaqāča barildužu bain büküi-dür
sentences.l: Jüchi Cha'adai two collar-by grappling standing being-when,
sentences.i: While Jüchi and Cha'adai were standing, the two of them locked together by the collar,
sentences.n: Qojar ‘two’ follows the pair it counts (Ming 兩箇). Žaqāča is žaqa + ablative -ača written long (Ming 領行); barildužu is bari- ‘seize’ + reciprocal -ldu- + converb (Ming 共拿着). Bain büküi-dür: bai- ‘stand’ + converb -n, then bü- ‘be’ + -küi + -dür ‘when being’: a standing, while-it-was clause.

sentences.t: Žuči-jin γar-ača Boγ̇orču tatažu Čaγ̇adai-jin γar-ača Muqali tatažu
sentences.l: Jüchi-of hand-from Bo'orchu pulling, Cha'adai-of hand-from Muqali pulling,
sentences.i: Bo'orchu pulled Jüchi away by the hand, and Muqali pulled Cha'adai away by the hand,
sentences.n: Tatažu (Ming 扯着 ‘pulling’) is tata- ‘pull’ + converb; the ablative γar-ača (Ming 手行) is ‘from the hand’, here ‘by the hand, from the grip’. The glossary also notes that tata- elsewhere has a different Ming sense (做妾着), so I rest this one only on the context and the Ming 扯着 here.

sentences.t: büküi-dür Čiṅgis Qaγan sonosču sem saγ̇un bi.

morph.gloss: is (Ming 有; perhaps a short form of bü-) [有]

sentences.l: Being-when, Chinggis Qaγan hearing silent sitting is.
sentences.i: and Chinggis Qahan sat there listening, silent.
sentences.n: The unit finishes the ‘while’ of the two preceding: büküi-dür ‘when being’ again, then sonosču ‘hearing’ (sonos- + converb -ču), sem (Ming 噤聲 ‘hush, hold the voice’), saγ̇un (saγ̇u- ‘sit’ + -n) and bi (the Ming 有, ‘is/was’). I render sem as ‘silent’ though the Ming means to make no sound; the word itself is not known elsewhere to me.

sentences.t: Tende Kökösös žeġün eteġed baižu ügülerün:
sentences.l: There Kökösös left side standing saying:
sentences.i: Then Kökösös, standing at the left, said:
sentences.n: Žeġün ‘left’ and eteġed ‘side’ (Ming 左, 邊) are two nouns together, ‘left side’; eteġed carries a -d that may be a plural or part of the stem. Kökösös is in the Ming 人名 ‘a man’s name’. The Ming says only ‘left side’ (左 邊); where he stood in relation to Chinggis is not given. The stance is in the Mongol (baižu ‘standing’).

sentences.t: "Čaγ̇adai jakin jaγ̇araju či.

morph.gloss: to hurry (stem inferred from Ming 忙) [忙有]
ending (uncertain: a converb in -ju, though the Ming 忙有 ‘is hurried’ reads it as a predicate)

sentences.l: "Cha'adai why hasty you.
sentences.i: “Cha'adai, why are you so hasty?
sentences.n: Kökösös’s speech opens with Shiratori’s mark at Čaγ̇adai and runs as one quotation to the end of §254 (büleġe"); inside it the mother’s thoughts are set in single quotes in `i` only. Jakin ‘why, how’ (Ming 為甚 ‘for what’), jaγ̇araju (Ming 忙有 ‘hurried, busy’) is a converb-like form (-ju) of jaγ̇ara-; či ‘you’ closes the question.

sentences.t: Qān ečige čin-u köġüd-ün dotora čima-dāča erežü büleġe.

morph.gloss: qan, ruler, sovereign (the short form) [皇帝]
ablative: from (long form of -da-ača; oblique stem čima-)
to look to, hope for (stem inferred; Ming 指望) [指望着]

sentences.l: Qan father your sons-of among you-from hoping was.
sentences.i: Father Qan was looking to you among his sons.
sentences.n: Čin-u (Ming 你的) is ‘your’, and I take it as agreeing with Qān ečige, ‘your father the Qan’, though in the Ming it could belong with köġüd-ün (‘your sons’). Erežü (Ming 指望着 ‘relying on, hoping for’) is erе- ‘look to’ (inferred) + converb; čima-dāča is čima- (oblique of či) + ablative -dāča, written long. Dotora ‘among, inside’. So: ‘he was pinning his hopes on you, from among his sons’. Plausible, but the possessives are a knot I leave loose.

sentences.t: Tan-i törekü-jin urida hodutai teṅgeri horčižu büleġe.

morph.gloss: to go around, revolve (stem inferred; Ming 轉, the glossary has 繞) [轉着]

sentences.l: You born before star-having heaven turning was.
sentences.i: Before you were born, the starry heaven was turning.
sentences.n: Tan-i is the plural-polite ‘you’ in the accusative, tan-, + -i (Ming 您行), with the participle of töre- ‘be born’ in the genitive -jin (Ming 生的), ‘of the born, of the birth’: literally ‘you, of the birth, before’. Hodutai is hodun ‘star’ + -tai ‘having’ (the -n drops). Horčižu (Ming 轉着 ‘turning’; the glossary has 繞着) is the stem inferred from the Ming. Kökösös is describing the world before the Qan’s rise as turbulent, a picture the next units paint.

sentences.t: Olon ulus bulγa büleġe.
sentences.l: Many people rebellion was.
sentences.i: The many peoples were in revolt.
sentences.n: Bulγa ‘revolt, disorder’ (Ming 反 ‘rebel’) is used elsewhere, with the Ming 厮殺, for fighting; here Ming 反, so ‘revolt’.

sentences.t: Oron-dur(i)-jan ülü oron olžalaldun büleġe.

morph.gloss: bed, bedding [睡臥 裏 自的行]

sentences.l: Bed-own-in not entering, mutual-plundering was.
sentences.i: They did not go into their beds; they plundered one another.
sentences.n: Oron-dur(i)-jan (Ming 睡臥裏 自的行) is oron ‘bed, bedding’ + dative-locative -dur + Shiratori’s (i) + reflexive -jan; ülü oron is ‘not entering’ (oro- ‘enter’, converb -n, Ming 入) — the words are close but separate; olžalaldun is olža ‘plunder’ + -la- + reciprocal -ldu- + -n, ‘plundering one another’ (Ming 相劫財). The first oron is the bed, the second a verb: the same spelling twice, with two senses. That is my reading.

sentences.t: Körišütei etügen körbežü büleġe.

morph.gloss: skin, surface (stem inferred; Ming 地皮) [地皮(有的)]
to overturn (stem inferred; Ming 翻) [翻着]

sentences.l: Earth-skin-having earth turning-over was.
sentences.i: The skin of the earth was being turned over.
sentences.n: Körišütei (Ming 地皮有的) is körisü ‘skin’ (inferred) + -tei ‘having’, the earth that has a skin; etügen is the Earth goddess (Mother Etügen, Ming 地). Körbežü (Ming 翻着 ‘turning over’), from a stem körbe-. Read together: ‘the skin-bearing earth was being overturned’; the sense is of the whole earth in upheaval.

sentences.t: Gür ulus bulγa büleġe.
sentences.l: All people rebellion was.
sentences.i: All peoples were in revolt.
sentences.n: Gür (Ming 普 ‘universal’), glossed as ‘all, whole’ in gür ulus, the form in which it works as an adjective in the glossary; it can also be the title in Gür-Qan.

sentences.t: Künžile-deġen ülü kebten körüleldün büleġe.

morph.gloss: quilt, bedcovering [被兒裏 自的行]
attack, assault (stem inferred; Ming 攻) [相攻]

sentences.l: Quilt-own-in not lying, mutual-attacking was.
sentences.i: They did not lie in their quilts; they attacked one another.
sentences.n: Künžile-deġen (Ming 被兒裏 自的行) is künžile ‘quilt’ + the reflexive-possessive dative -deġen, ‘in one’s own quilt’. Körüleldün is körü ‘attack’ (inferred) + -le- + reciprocal -ldü- + -n (Ming 相攻), parallel to olžalaldun above (olža + -la- + -ldu- + -n).

sentences.t: Teimü Čaγ-tur küsežü ese jabuba-že.

morph.gloss: to go, walk [行了 也者︀]

sentences.l: Such time-at desiring not has-gone-indeed.
sentences.i: In such a time they did not go about wishing.
sentences.n: Here begin six short clauses, three pairs, which I could not make quite plain. Küsežü (Ming 思想着 ‘desiring, wanting’) is küse- + converb; ese jabuba-že is ‘did not go’ with the assertion -že (Ming 行了也者); the Ming (思想着 … 不曾 行了也者) gives ‘desiring … did not go’. The object of küse- is not given. My rendering follows the Ming and says only that.

sentences.t: Kürülčeküi-dür bolba-že.

words.reading: 古舌魯勒扯恢-突︀舌兒 Kürülčeküi-dür

sentences.l: Meeting-at became-indeed.
sentences.i: When they met, it came to be so.
sentences.n: Kürülčeküi-dür is kürü- (inferred) + reciprocal -lče- (Ming 相遇 ‘meet each other’) + participle -küi + dative-locative -dür, ‘at meeting’. Bolba-že is ‘became’ (Ming 做了 也者; the glossary has 肻做了 ‘agreed to be’ for other uses); the contrast with the line before is the point: they did not go out wanting it, but when met, it came to be done. The fighting at which it came to be is implied, not named.

sentences.t: Buruγ̇udču ese jabuba.

morph.gloss: to flee, take cover (stem uncertain; Ming 逃躱) [躱着]

sentences.l: Fleeing not went.
sentences.i: They did not flee.
sentences.n: Buruγ̇udču (Ming 躱着 ‘hiding, dodging’; the glossary has 逃躱 ‘flee and hide’, from which `i` takes ‘flee’) is a converb in -ču after a consonant; jabuba (Ming 行了), unlike jabuba-že above, takes no -že in this line.

sentences.t: Bulγalduqui-dur bolba-že.

words.reading: 不勒中合勒都︀中灰-突︀舌兒 Bulγalduqui-dur

glyphs.s: 不勒中合勒都︀中灰-突︀舌兒

sentences.l: Fighting-at became-indeed.
sentences.i: When they fought one another, it came to be so.
sentences.n: Bulγalduqui-dur is bulγa- ‘contend’ + reciprocal -ldu- + participle -qui + dative-locative -dür ‘when fighting one another’ (Ming 厮殺時).

sentences.t: Amaražu ese jabuba-že.

morph.gloss: to love one another (stem inferred; Ming 相愛) [相愛着]
to go, walk [行了 也者︀]

sentences.l: Loving not went-indeed.
sentences.i: They did not go about loving one another.
sentences.n: Amaražu (Ming 相愛着 ‘loving one another’), amara- ‘love’ (inferred) + converb -žu.

sentences.t: Alalduqui-dur bolba-že.

words.reading: 阿剌勒都︀中灰-突︀舌兒 Alalduqui-dur

sentences.l: Killing-one-another-at became-indeed.
sentences.i: When they slew one another, it came to be so.
sentences.n: Alalduqui-dur (Ming 厮殺時) is ala- ‘kill’ + reciprocal -ldu- + participle -qui + dative-locative, ‘at killing one another’. The six clauses together describe the lawless age before the rising of Chinggis; the pairs and their -že are a closing refrain.

sentences.t: Boγda qatun eke-jüġen tosun duran qoruγ̇ulžu sün žürügen edeġülžü ügülemüi.

morph.gloss: sacred, holy; here wise, venerable [賢明的]
to cause to congeal (stem inferred from Ming 敎凝) [敎凝了着]
to loosen, dissolve (stem inferred from Ming 解) [解了着]

sentences.l: Wise lady mother-own, butter heart-own having-made-congeal, milk heart having-loosened, says.
sentences.i: Your mother, the wise lady, spoke, congealing her butter-heart and dissolving her milk-heart.
sentences.n: The tosun duran and sün žürügen are two fixed images, ‘butter’ and ‘milk’ with the heart and the will; the Ming reads 蘇油 心 敎凝了着 ‘made the butter-heart congeal’ and 乳 心 解了着 ‘loosened the milk-heart’. `i` keeps to the Ming’s ‘congealing’ and ‘dissolving’; whether it is a firming of will and a softening of heart, as I suppose, the Ming does not say, and the sense could be reversed. Eke-jüġen is ‘own mother’ with the reflexive -jüġen; boγda ‘sacred’, here ‘wise, venerable’ (Ming 賢明). ‘Your’ is my addition; the text has ‘their own mother’.

sentences.t: Či büleġen-eče büled mün.

morph.gloss: warm (stem uncertain; Ming 溫) [溫的行]

sentences.l: You warm-from suddenly only.
sentences.i: You, from warmth, suddenly — only that.
sentences.n: I cannot parse this fragment. Či ‘you’; büleġen-eče (Ming 溫的行 ‘warm’) as ‘from the warm’; büled (Ming 忽然 ‘suddenly’); mün ‘just, only’ (Ming 只). It follows the clause on the mother above and precedes the questions about birth below, and I can give only the words.

sentences.t: Keġeli-dēče ese-ü töreleġei ta.

morph.gloss: not (negates a past action) [不曾 麽]

sentences.l: Belly-from not-?  born you.
sentences.i: Were you not born from the belly?
sentences.n: Keġeli-dēče is keġeli ‘belly’ (Ming 肚皮) + ablative written long; ese-ü is ‘not’ + the question particle (Ming 不曾麽 ‘was it not?’); töreleġei is töre- ‘be born’ + -leġei ‘was’ (the glossary’s ‘was born’); ta ‘you (plural)’.

sentences.t: Qalaγ̇un-ača qalad γaγča γaqunaγ-ača ese-ü γarulaγ̇a ta.

words.reading: 中合中忽納中合察 γaqunaγ-ača

morph.gloss: not (negates a past action) [不曾 麽]

sentences.l: Heat-from suddenly only afterbirth-from not-? came-out you.
sentences.i: From the heat, suddenly, from the afterbirth alone — did you not come out?
sentences.n: Qalaγ̇un-ača (Ming 熱的行) ‘from the hot’, qalad ‘suddenly’ (Ming 忽然 here; the glossary has 猛然) and γaγča ‘only’ repeat the previous unit’s warm/suddenly/only fragment; γaqunaγ (Ming 衣胞) is the afterbirth; γarulaγ̇a ‘came out’ (Ming 出來來; the ending -laγ̇a uncertain). Taken together the two units are a taunt, ‘did you not all come from the one belly, the one afterbirth?’ — that is my reading, not a certain one.

sentences.t: žürügen-eče töregsen eke-jüġen čimadγaγ̇asu činar in-ü žekirčü žaliraγ̇uluγ̇asu ülü boli.

morph.gloss: to be strange (stem inferred; Ming 敎恠) [敎恠呵]

words.reading: 札里舌剌兀魯阿速 žaliraγ̇uluγ̇asu

morph.gloss: to sigh (stem inferred; Ming 敎息) [敎息呵]
will do, be acceptable (Ming 中; form uncertain) [中]

sentences.l: Heart-from born mother-own if-made-wonder, feeling her cold-becoming, if-made-sigh not will-do.
sentences.i: If you make the mother who bore you from her heart wonder at you, and make her sigh with her feeling chilled, it will not do.
sentences.n: Čimadγaγ̇asu (Ming 敎恠呵 ‘if made to wonder’) is čima- ‘be strange’ + causative -dγa- + conditional (a stem I infer); žaliraγ̇uluγ̇asu (Ming 敎息呵 ‘if made to sigh’) is žalira- + causative -γ̇ul- + conditional. Ülü boli (Ming 不 中 ‘will not do’). Činar ‘feeling, character’ (Ming 情); in-ü ‘her’. Žürügen-eče töregsen is ‘born from the heart’, which I treat as a figure (the mother’s heart), though ‘heart’ might also be a plain ‘inner’.

sentences.t: Keġeli-dēče töregsen eke-jüġen gemüriġülüġesü genüġer in-ü gegeġesü ülü boli.

words.reading: 格木舌里兀魯額速 gemüriġülüġesü

morph.gloss: to resent (stem inferred; Ming 怨) [敎怨呵]
to clear, dissolve (stem inferred; Ming 消) [消呵]
will do, be acceptable (Ming 中; form uncertain) [中]

sentences.l: Belly-from born mother-own if-made-resent, resentment her if-cleared not will-do.
sentences.i: If you make the mother who bore you from her belly resentful, no clearing will dispel her bitterness.
sentences.n: A parallel to the sentence above with keġeli ‘belly’ for žürügen ‘heart’. Gemüriġülüġesü is gemüri- ‘resent’ (Ming 怨, inferred) + causative -ġül- + conditional -ġesü; genüġer (Ming 怨悔 ‘resentment, regret’) is a noun; gegeġesü (Ming 消呵 ‘if it dissolves, clears’) from gege-, the conditional. Ülü boli again ‘will not do’. Genüġer is not clear to me beyond the Ming.

sentences.t: Qān ečige tan-u Qamuγ ulus-i baiγ̇ulurun

morph.gloss: qan, ruler, sovereign (the short form) [皇帝]

sentences.l: Qan father your all people-(object) when-establishing,
sentences.i: When Father Qan was setting up all your people,
sentences.n: A long unit of Kökösös’s speech breaks here into smaller pieces. The thread: when the Qan was raising the nation (baiγ̇ulurun, bai- ‘stand’ + causative -γ̇ul- + -urun, Ming 敎立時 ‘when establishing’), he and your mother bore every hardship. The things he did without are listed in the next units. Tan-u ‘your (plural)’ (Ming 您的) here speaks to Cha'adai and his brothers together.

sentences.t: qara teriġü-ben qantuqalažu qara čisu-ban nambuγalažu

morph.gloss: to carry up on the horse (stem inferred from the Ming 馬上指着) [馬上指着]
to put in a leather pail (stem inferred from the Ming 皮桶盛着) [皮桶盛着]

sentences.l: Black head-own on-horse-carrying, black blood-own leather-pail-putting,
sentences.i: carrying his black head upon his horse and his black blood in a leather pail,
sentences.n: Qara teriġü-ben (Ming 黑頭 自的行) is ‘one’s own black head’ (why ‘black’, the Ming does not say); qantuqalažu (Ming 馬上指着 ‘holding up upon the horse’) and nambuγalažu (Ming 皮桶盛着 ‘put in a leather pail’) are verbs I infer from the Ming and cannot test. Both are standing images for risking one’s life. -ben and -ban are the reflexive-possessive by vowel harmony.

sentences.t: qara nidü-ben hirmes ülü kin
sentences.l: Black eye-own turning not doing,
sentences.i: not so much as turning his black eyes,
sentences.n: Hirmes (Ming 轉) is ‘a turn’ or ‘blink’ (the glossary gives both); ülü kin is ‘not doing’ with ki- ‘do’ + -n. The sense, ‘not even blinking’, is the glossary’s second reading.

sentences.t: qabtaγai čiki-ben dere-dür ülü talbin
sentences.l: Flat ear-own pillow-on not putting,
sentences.i: not laying his flat ear on a pillow,
sentences.n: Qabtaγai (Ming 匾 ‘flat’) is an adjective; čiki-ben ‘his ear’; dere-dür ‘on the pillow’ (dere ‘pillow’ + dative-locative, Ming 枕行). Talbin is talbi- ‘put down’ + converb.

sentences.t: qanču-ban dereležü qormai-ban debüsčü

morph.gloss: lapel, front of the robe [衣襟 自的行]
to spread out (stem inferred; Ming 鋪) [鋪着]

sentences.l: Sleeve-own pillowing, lapel-own spreading,
sentences.i: making a pillow of his sleeve, spreading his lapel for a bed,
sentences.n: Dereležü is dere ‘pillow’ + -le- + converb, ‘making a pillow of’ (Ming 枕着); debüsčü is debüs- ‘spread’ (stem inferred; Ming 鋪着) + -čü. Qanču ‘sleeve’ and qormai ‘lapel’ (Ming 袖, 衣襟).

sentences.t: šilusun(i)-jan undalažu šigi-jan qonaγlažu

morph.gloss: to quench thirst (Ming 解渴) [解渴着]
tooth-gap meat (sense from the Ming 牙縫中肉 only) [牙縫中肉]
to take as a night’s meal (Ming 當宿食) [當宿食]

sentences.l: Saliva-own thirst-quenching, tooth-gap-meat-own as-night-meal,
sentences.i: quenching his thirst with his own spit, making a night’s meal of what stuck between his teeth,
sentences.n: Šilusun(i)-jan (Ming 涎 自的行) is spittle with Shiratori’s (i); undalažu (Ming 解渴着) from undala- ‘quench thirst’. Šigi-jan (Ming 牙縫中肉 ‘meat between the teeth’) and qonaγlažu (Ming 當宿食 ‘as a night’s lodging meal’) are hard in the Mongol; I follow the Ming.

sentences.t: maṅlai-jin kölesün ula-dur kürtele ula-jin kölesün maṅlai-tur γartala

morph.gloss: sole of the foot [腳底 上]

sentences.l: Brow-of sweat sole-on reaching, sole-of sweat brow-on rising,
sentences.i: until the sweat of his brow reached his soles and the sweat of his soles rose to his brow,
sentences.n: Maṅlai ‘brow, forehead’ (Ming 額), kölesün ‘sweat’ (Ming 汗), ula ‘sole’ (Ming 腳底); kürtele is kür- ‘reach’ + -tele ‘until’, and γartala (Ming 直上 ‘straight up’) is the matching -tala form of γar- ‘go up’: ‘until reaching … until going up’. The sweat that ran down and up is a hyperbole for effort.

sentences.t: ölümlen kičijen jabuqui čaγ-tur eke tan-u qamtu-bar žoboldurun

morph.gloss: to suffer, toil (stem inferred; Ming 辛苦) [辛苦時]

sentences.l: Forward carefully when-going, mother your together hardship-when,
sentences.i: going forward with care, and your mother, together with him, in hardship,
sentences.n: Ölümlen (Ming 向前 ‘forward’) and kičijen (Ming 謹愼 ‘careful’) are adverbs; jabuqui čaγ-tur is ‘at the time of going’; eke tan-u qamtu-bar (Ming 母 您的 同行) ‘your mother, with’ — qamtu ‘together’ + instrumental -bar; žoboldurun (Ming 辛苦時 ‘time of hardship’) is žobol- ‘suffer’ + -dur-un. A stem for žobol- is inferred.

sentences.t: qoraitala boγtalažu qoγ̇ožitala büseležü niġitaitala boγtolažu niduratala büseležü

morph.gloss: to be tight (stem inferred; Ming 緊) [緊]
to be short (stem inferred; Ming 短) [短]
to be tight (stem inferred; Ming 緊) [緊]
to be tight (stem inferred; Ming 緊) [緊]

sentences.l: Tight head-dressing, short belting, tight head-dressing, tight belting,
sentences.i: tightening her headdress, drawing in her belt, tightening her headdress, tightening her belt,
sentences.n: The suffixes -tala/-itala make four degrees of tightness (qoraitala, qoγ̇ožitala, niġitaitala, niduratala; Ming 緊, 短, 緊, 緊 ‘tight, short, tight, tight’), each followed by a verb of dressing: boγtalažu (boγta, the married woman’s headdress as in the glossary; this Ming says 梳頭着 ‘dressing the hair’) and büseležü (büse ‘belt’, Ming 繫着, 繫腰着). Boγtolažu in the third pair is the same verb with an alternate spelling. The stems qoγ̇ožai-, niġi- and nidura- and the splits of qoγ̇ožitala and niġitaitala are inferred from the Ming and uncertain. The picture is of a woman going hungry, drawing in her clothes; neither Mongol nor Ming says why, and I leave the reason to the later units.

sentences.t: tan(i)-jan ösgerün žalgqui žaγ̇ura

morph.gloss: you (plural polite, stem tan-) [您 自的行]
to raise, rear (Ming 敎長) [敎長時]
to swallow (stem inferred; Ming 嚥) [嚥]

sentences.l: You-own raising-when swallowing interval,
sentences.i: as she raised you, and in the interval of swallowing,
sentences.n: Tan(i)-jan (Ming 您 自的行) is the plural-polite ‘you’ (stem tan-) with Shiratori’s (i) and the reflexive; ösgerün is ösge- ‘raise’ (causative of ös- ‘grow’; Ming 敎長 ‘cause to grow’) + -rün; žalgqui (Ming 嚥 ‘swallow’) with žaγ̇ura ‘in the midst’ (Ming 其間).

sentences.t: žarim(i)-jan ögčü qoγ̇olai-jan qučižu qotola(i)-jan ögčü

morph.gloss: to swallow (stem inferred; Ming 咽) [咽着]

sentences.l: Half-own giving, throat-own swallowing, all-own giving,
sentences.i: giving half of her own, swallowing it down her own throat, giving all of her own,
sentences.n: Žarim(i)-jan (Ming 一半 自的行) is žarim ‘half’ with Shiratori’s (i). Qoγ̇olai is the throat, qučižu (Ming 咽着) ‘swallowing’. Qotola(i)-jan (Ming 都自的行) ‘all of it’. As in the glossary’s entries, ögčü is ög- ‘give’ + -čü after a consonant. The two ögčü make a pair; whether the mother gave the half to the children and swallowed the rest herself is my reading of the Ming.

sentences.t: qoγ̇osun jabuqui büleġei.
sentences.l: Empty going was.
sentences.i: she went about with an empty stomach.
sentences.n: Qoγ̇osun ‘empty’ (Ming 空) with jabuqui ‘going’ (Ming 行) and the past büleġei: ‘she was going empty’; ‘stomach’ is my addition. The end of the long sentence begun at Qān ečige tan-u.

sentences.t: Egemēče tan-u tatažu ere-lüġe sačaγ̇un ken-e bolγaqu.

morph.gloss: shoulder (stem inferred; Ming 肩甲) [肩甲行]

sentences.l: Shoulder-from your pulling, man-with alike how to-be-made.
sentences.i: ‘How should I bring you up, by the shoulder, to stand level with men?
sentences.n: This is the mother’s own thought inside Kökösös’s speech; Shiratori prints no marks, and I put it in single quotes in `i` for sense. Read the next unit as its pair. Egemēče (Ming 肩甲行 ‘from the shoulder’) with tatažu ‘pulling’ (as the Ming 扯着); ere-lüġe is ere ‘man’ + comitative ‘together with a man’ (Ming 人 一同); sačaγ̇un (Ming 齊等 ‘level, alike’), ken-e bolγaqu (Ming 怎生 做的麽): ken-e glossed ‘how’ here, from the Ming, bolγaqu ‘to be made’. The sense of the whole is ‘by what means shall they be made equal to men?’ Not fully secure.

sentences.t: Küžüġün-eče tan-u tatažu küġün-lüġe sačaγ̇un ken-e bolγaqu keġežü bui

morph.gloss: is (particle; the Ming leaves it blank)

sentences.l: Nape-from your pulling, person-with alike how to-be-made saying.
sentences.i: How should I bring you up, by the neck, to stand level with other people?’ so she said to herself.
sentences.n: The partner of the sentence before: küžüġün-eče (Ming 項頸行 ‘from the neck’) for egemēče, küġün-lüġe ‘with a person’ for ere-lüġe, and the closing keġežü (‘saying’). Bui (Ming blank) follows; it looks like a particle ‘is’ and I leave it unrendered. The last word of one sentence and the first of the next can be hard to place here.

sentences.t: tan-u arilγažu burbi tan-u ergüġülžü ere-jin egem-tür aγta-jin qarγam-tur kürgežü

words.reading: 中合舌兒甘-突︀舌兒 qarγam-tur

morph.gloss: to bring to, deliver (kür- ‘reach’ made causative) [敎到着]

sentences.l: Your washing-clean, heel your lifting, man-of shoulder-on, gelding-of haunch-on bringing,
sentences.i: She washed you clean and lifted up your heels, and brought you to a man’s shoulder and a gelding’s haunch,
sentences.n: Arilγažu (Ming 敎淨着) from aril- ‘be clean’ + causative -γa- + converb, ‘cleansing’; ergüġülžü (Ming 敎擡起着) from ergü- ‘lift’ + causative -ġül-. Burbi (Ming 腳後根 ‘heel’) is a noun without a case, so ‘lifting your heels’ is the Ming’s sense, not a certain parse. Egem-tür and qarγam-tur (Ming 肩行, 後胯行) are ‘on the shoulder’ and ‘on the haunch’; aγta-jin ‘of a gelding’; kürgežü ‘bringing to’ (kürge-). The picture is height: she brought them up to a man’s shoulder, a horse’s hindquarters.

sentences.t: edöġe tan-u-γ̇an sai üžesü keġen sedkižü ese-ü amui.

morph.gloss: optative, first person: let me (like -suγai; Ming 見我, with no 呵)

sentences.l: Now your-own well if-I-see saying thinking not-? is.
sentences.i: Did she not think, ‘Now let me see you well!’
sentences.n: Tan-u-γ̇an (Ming (您)自(的)行) is ta ‘you’ + genitive -u + the reflexive -γ̇an, three suffixes on one stem, glossed ‘your own’; sai ‘well, good’; üžesü (Ming 見我 ‘I see, let me see’) from üje- ‘see’ + -sü, a first-person form like -suγai above, not a conditional (the Ming has no 呵); keġen sedkižü ‘saying, thinking’; ese-ü amui, ‘is it not so?’, a rhetorical ‘did she not’. A noun may be missing between tan-u-γ̇an and sai.

sentences.t: Boγda qatun bidan-u naran metü gegeġen naγ̇ur metü delger sedkiltü büleġe" keġebe.

morph.gloss: sacred, holy; here wise, venerable [賢明]
we, us (inclusive: you and I; stem bidan- before case endings) [咱的]

sentences.l: Wise lady our sun like bright, lake like broad heart-having was" he-said.
sentences.i: Our wise lady had a heart as bright as the sun and as broad as a lake.” So he spoke.
sentences.n: The closing: boγda qatun again (as Jesüi was ‘qatun’ before; here it is the mother); bidan-u ‘our’ (Ming 咱的, inclusive), naran ‘sun’ with metü ‘like’, gegeġen ‘bright’ (Ming 明); naγ̇ur ‘lake’ (Ming 海, ‘sea’) with metü, delger ‘wide’ (Ming 寬洪); sedkiltü is sedkil ‘heart’ + -tü ‘having’ (Ming 心有的), then büleġe" closes the quotation and keġebe ‘said’ closes the whole section. The tail of the chronicle’s §254 thus ends on a simile, as Jesüi’s speech did on two.
